$comment: Per-scene physical cast declarations for tools/check-line-presence.mjs.
WHY THIS IS HAND-WRITTEN, NOT DERIVED: the codebase stages characters at
least four different ways -- src/mansion/cast.js's post() registry,
src/bing/family.js's FAMILY table + populateFamily(), src/heist/cast.js's
HEIST_CREW_IDS, src/enolasquatch/crew.js's createCrew(), src/golf's
buildGallery()/buildFoursome(), direct `new Npc(...)` calls, and plain
`makeFigure()` calls with no registry at all. No single grep pattern finds
'who has a body in this scene' across all of them without also matching
unrelated things (wardrobe tables, face-photo tables, prop names). So each
row below was seeded by hand, reading the scene's own cast/mount source --
see `sourceFiles` on each entry -- rather than guessed from a pattern.
`staged` is the list of voice PROFILE ids (assets/sfx/manifest.json's
`voices` block keys) that have an actual built body somewhere in the
scene. A voice not in this list, and not covered by an exemption in
tools/check-line-presence.mjs, is reported as a violation: lines with
nobody standing there to say them.
`sceneVoiceExemptions` covers a voice that legitimately has NO body in
THIS scene for its entire run -- always heard over a radio, an intercom or
a phone rather than ever appearing -- even though its cue prefix belongs
to the scene. Each one cites the source line that proves it. This is
different from the global phone/radio/PA prefix exemptions in the checker
(vo.call.*, vo.machine.*, vo.news.*, radio.*): those catch cues that were
AUTHORED as a call/broadcast. These catch a scene's own cue prefix being
used for a character who the scene's own code establishes is contacted
electronically for the whole mission.
KEEP THIS BY HAND when a scene's roster changes -- it is data, not a
generated file, and nothing regenerates it. If a new mission adds a
speaking character, add their voice id to `staged` (or a dated violation
will appear the moment their first line is written).

scenes.label: PROJECT SILENT SQUATCH

sceneVoiceExemptions.labcomputer: The laboratory's own annunciator -- script.js's SPEAKERS.LAB_COMPUTER docstring: 'Flat, synthetic, indifferent.' A PA voice with no body by design, the same class as vo.machine./vo.news.

scenes.notes: Snow ('snow', 5 lines) staged as of the 8-6 punch-list fix (S10): cast.js's snow errand (cast.js:982-1100) brings his body into the lab through the pier opening for the script.js:695 'snow.arrives' stage, so snowIntercom's first three lines play over the intercom while he is on his way and the last two are said in the room. His permanent foyer post covers snowFoyer/snowIdle as before. Was this checker's original known offender, reported until the fix landed.

scenes.label: MANSION UNDER SIEGE
scenes.notes: ensemble.js's ROSTER fields the whole family as defenders (lou, booski, rippinflow, snow, shubenator, eric, aubbie, irish, deathmegatron, numbskull, hogmama, captain_lou_sasole) plus guard_0/1/2/wounded on the mansion-guard voice. Every siege voice resolves to a body.

scenes.label: The HotDog Incident
scenes.notes: buildHotDogParty() seats the whole FAMILY roster (minus the two it filters, which it then re-adds explicitly) plus Lou, Billy HotDog, Aubbie and Sauce by name. Sauce ('sauce') has no lines in this bank so it is absent from `staged` on purpose -- add it back if a Sauce line is ever authored here.

scenes.label: The Enola Squatch
scenes.notes: crew.js's createCrew() builds exactly four men (sasole/irish/numbskull/shubes) and says so in its own header: 'Big Uncle Lou is not on this aeroplane.' 'lou1' (4 lines) is DELIBERATELY NOT in `staged`. Two of its four lines ('call.opening') are the pre-flight phone call and are exempted by cue-name in the checker. The other two ('arrival.lou') are NOT exempted: MissionController.js's own comment calls the epilogue 'the one deliberate stub... no populated hangar/crowd-of-Family-NPCs scene' -- Lou's arrival line plays over an empty apron. A second Snow-in-lab, caught by this tool.

sceneVoiceExemptions.lou: HEIST_CREW_IDS (src/heist/cast.js) is prospect/snow/rippinflow/shubenator/deathmegatron/numbskull -- Lou is never one of the five crew bodies. script.js's own comment on HEIST_PENDING_DIALOGUE confirms it: 'He is on the radio for the job and he is the last voice in the safehouse' -- every lou_radio_*/lou_call/lou_debrief_* cue is the crew hearing him over a connection, never a body in the room.

scenes.label: Bada Bing
scenes.notes: cast.js's populate() builds the floor staff (doorman/bouncer/hallGuard/security -> 'doorman' voice per script.js's VOICE_BY_SCOPE, bartender, dealer, dj -> 'announcer', margo, plus generic 'regular'/'patron'/'tabler'/'stander' background bodies that carry the 'npc-male' ambient lines) and family.js's FAMILY table seats the rest by name, including James Blond ('blond', license-to-grill-runtime.js's makeBlond()) and Aubbie/Sauce off the clock. NOTE, not a violation: vo.bj.dealer.* cues carry voice 'uncle' while VOICE_BY_SCOPE casts the scope as 'dealer' and a second cue family (vo.bing.blackjack.dealer.*, vo.bing.full.dealer.*) carries voice 'dealer' for what reads like the same blackjack table -- two profile ids for one body. Both resolve to the same physically staged dealer NPC, so neither is a presence violation, but it looks like the kind of casting drift PLAYTEST-PUNCH-LIST.md S5 describes and is worth a human look.

scenes.label: Silver Pines
scenes.notes: The foursome (Lou, Rippinflow, Eric, the player) plays the round; hole3.js's GALLERY places Booski/Shubenator/DeathMegatron/Numbskull/Snow at the clubhouse for hole 3, built by terrain.js's buildGallery(). vo.call.lou.golf.*/vo.machine.lou.*_day.* are already covered by the checker's global phone/machine prefix exemption; listed here only so their cues resolve to this scene instead of tripping the 'unmapped cue' guard.

scenes.label: The Silver Room
scenes.notes: cast.js's populate() builds Vinny/the doorman ('doorman'), 'manager', 'waiter' (plus mover1/mover2/server<N> on the same voice) and 'the host'; Ape is spread in as the exact Bing FAMILY figure (identifySilverApe()). The single 'announcer' line ('...the Silver Room is proud... the Midnight Pines') is the room's own host introducing the act on stage, not an offscreen PA.

scenes.label: The Silver Case
scenes.notes: cast/cast.js builds ape, chester, Deke and Winston (both voiced 'npc-male' per dialogue/script.js's VOICE_OF) and Pruitt (hidden until revealed, also 'npc-male').

scenes.label: NO WAKE
scenes.notes: boat.cast.{lou,booski,willy,irish} are built and moved through the whole scene in main.js -- the cabin confrontation, the execution, the wrap and the deck departure.

scenes.label: The Beef Run

sceneVoiceExemptions.caib-radio: script.js's own SPEAKERS entry names it 'CAIB RADIO' -- air-traffic-control chatter over the aircraft radio, never a body in the scene.
sceneVoiceExemptions.lookout: The line's own authored text is tagged '(radio, urgent)' (script.js: 'Motor. Two valleys over, coming this way.') -- a lookout calling in over the radio, not standing in frame.

scenes.notes: makeLou()==Sasole ('lou2'), makeOldStove(), makeCecilio() are all built and staged; makeAssociate() is built immediately before the 'end.crew' beat plays ('Sasole. You're green.').

scenes.label: Jerky Motel
scenes.notes: actors.js's identity presets build snow/rico/chino directly.

scenes.label: Squatch Graveyard
scenes.notes: Snow is a built Npc in the plot. 'echo' ('Hey, guys? I am still alive down here.') is the one squatch buried alive at the 'echo' plot -- he has no visible body by the scene's own joke, but world.js gives his exact grave a dedicated, audio-synced rumble effect (`echoSoil`/`startEchoRumble`) at the same spot the line comes from, which is the physical staging this scene has for a man underground. Treated as staged rather than a violation; flag this row for a human if that reasoning does not hold up.

scenes.label: Initiation
scenes.notes: npc.js's ROSTER seats the whole circle by voice; main.js's PROSPECT_NAMES line builds 'PROSPECT ONE' (voice 'doorman' per dialogue.js's VOICE_OF) as a standing figure with a nameplate, first in the initiation line.

scenes.label: Apartment and shared
scenes.notes: Every prefix here except vo.margo.* is exclusively the player's own muttering (voice 'player', globally exempt -- see the checker). Margo is built once per campaign load in apartment.js ('Built in every chapter and shown by the cutscene') and shown/hidden by chapter, not rebuilt per scene.
